newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields creep up,enter quiet period.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields creep up,enter quiet period.

text.p: *Australian bond yields were marginally higher, reflecting weaker U.S. Treasuries and as the market began squaring up ahead of Friday's U.S. labour force data and Monday's local holiday.
Australian bond yields were marginally higher, reflecting weaker U.S. Treasuries and as the market began squaring up ahead of Friday's U.S. labour force data and Monday's local holiday.
"It's pretty dead so far and it looks like we are going to see a quiet couple of days," said one trader.

However, the market will be maintaining a constant vigil of the Reserve Bank's daily morning operations on the off chance that it announces a further policy easing after the suprise move to 5.5 percent on May 23.

There had been some speculation that the central bank would ease today during offshore trading hours, although this appeared to have more impact on the Australian dollar, which remains pegged below US$0.7600, rather than the debt market.

However, by 9.35 a.m. (2335 GMT) short-dated instruments had weakened further after the RBA had made no announcement on polic. September bill futures slipped to 94.58 and down four basis points equating to a cash rate of 5.42 percent.
There are no major local data due out until Wednesday's housing finance data and Thursday's labour force report.

The market underperform against the dollar bloc, notably against New Zealand, despite quarterly N.Z. private sector wages rising a slightly stronger than expected 1.1 percent for 3.6 percent in the year to February. The local yield curve continued to flatten in the absence of an RBA announcement on policy.
